sources.entry: qrcode - A pure Python QR Code generator.

summary.one_liner: A pure Python library and `qr` command-line script for generating QR codes as PNG, SVG, console ASCII, or (with Pillow) styled images.
summary.what_it_does: Generates QR codes from arbitrary data via the `qrcode.make` shortcut or the more configurable `QRCode` class, which exposes version, error correction level, box size, border, and fill/background colors. Output formats include PNG (through pypng by default, or Pillow when installed), SVG in several variants (rectangles, combined path, fragment), and text printed to the console. A `qr` command provides the same functionality from the shell, including ASCII output and writing to a file with `--output`. With the `[pil]` extra, styled images are supported, with rounded or circular module shapes, color masks such as radial gradients, and an embedded center image, though the README notes styled codes are not guaranteed to scan with every reader.
use_cases: generate QR codes in Python scripts
export QR codes as SVG for web pages
print QR codes as ASCII in a terminal
make branded QR codes with custom colors or a logo
generate QR codes from the command line
notable: Pure Python QR encoding with a PNG fallback that needs no Pillow
Multiple SVG output styles, including combined path and fragment variants
Styled images with module drawers (rounded, circle) and color masks
Optional embedded image in the center of the code
Command-line `qr` script with ASCII and file output
caveats: Styled QR codes may not scan reliably with all readers; the README advises testing and using high error correction
Styled image features require version 7.2 or later (SVG styled images require 7.4)
Advanced image styling needs the optional Pillow dependency installed with the [pil] extra
